data.text:
I have enough evidence to conclude. The chain is clear:

- **dns1.lan** (`/opt/primary-dns/config.yaml`) applies `ratelimit: 20` q/s over `ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24` — i.e. the *entire* 10.20.0.0/24 LAN shares one 20 q/s bucket. Its log shows exactly three brief episodes in recent days (02:14, 09:41, 13:02), each "back under limit" within ~30 s — matching "a few times a day, self-clearing".
- When dns1 drops queries, the client falls through to its second server **gw.lan**, whose unbound forwards `lan.` to dns1 but also has `private-address: 10.0.0.0/8` ("DNS rebinding protection"). Verified: `drill nas.lan @10.20.0.3` → answer 10.20.0.50, but the same name via gw's own resolver returns **NOERROR with ANSWER: 0**. So the fallback path silently yields "not found" for local names only; public internet names still resolve via the DoT forwarders, which is exactly what was reported.

data.cause: dns1's primary-dns rate limiter (ratelimit: 20 q/s applied at /24, so all of 10.20.0.0/24 shares one bucket) intermittently drops queries during short bursts; clients then fall back to their second server gw.lan, whose unbound private-address: 10.0.0.0/8 filtering suppresses the private answers for .lan, so local names return NOERROR-with-no-answer (ENOTFOUND) while internet names still resolve.
evidence: dns1 config sets a single aggregate limit for the whole LAN: `cat -n /opt/primary-dns/config.yaml` shows ratelimit: 20 with ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24, plus rewrites of *.lan / nas.lan to 10.20.0.50.

dns1 log shows brief, self-clearing drop events, matching 'a few times a day': `journalctl -u primary-dns` reports 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping 23/31/8 queries' at 02:14, 09:41 and 13:02, each followed by 'back under limit' within ~30s.
nas.lan resolves normally when dns1 is not limiting: `dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan` -> 10.20.0.50 (TTL 10).

The fallback server returns an empty answer for the same name: `dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan` and `drill nas.lan @127.0.0.1` on gw.lan both return status NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 — no error code, so getaddrinfo reports ENOTFOUND.

gw.lan explains why only local names are affected: `cat -n /var/unbound/unbound.conf` shows 'DNS rebinding protection' private-address: 10.0.0.0/8 together with forward-zone lan. -> 10.20.0.3, while '.' is forwarded over DoT to 1.1.1.2@853 / 9.9.9.9@853 with forward-first, so public names still resolve.
mon.lan client config confirms the two-server order that makes the silent-empty fallback visible: `cat /etc/resolv.conf` lists nameserver 10.20.0.3 then nameserver 10.20.0.1.
Both resolvers are healthy, so this is not a crashed service: unbound is running as pid 71204 (`service unbound status`) and primary-dns as pid 402 listening on 0.0.0.0:53 UDP+TCP (`ss -tulpn`).
data.recommendation: Raise dns1's rate limit so normal LAN bursts are not dropped — increase ratelimit well above 20 q/s and/or widen ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4 (e.g. /32) so each client gets its own bucket instead of the whole 10.20.0.0/24 sharing one. In the same change, stop gw.lan from masking local data: remove private-address: 10.0.0.0/8 for the forwarded lan. zone (or exempt the .lan forward-zone from the private-address filter), so that if dns1 is ever unreachable the fallback still returns the real address instead of an empty NOERROR. No reboot needed; a reload of both resolvers is enough.
data.detail: per-/24 ratelimit on primary-dns drops LAN bursts
